Facebook (FB) Market Valuation Declined While Js Capital Management Cut Stake; Star Group LP (SGU) Shareholder Locust Wood Capital Advisers Has Cut Its Stake by $341,260
May 27, 2018 - By Vivian Currie
Jonathan Soros decreased its stake in Facebook Inc (FB) by 3.42% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Js Capital Management Llc sold 4,000 shares as the company’s stock declined 14.10% with the market. The hedge fund run by Jonathan Soros held 113,000 shares of the technology company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $19.94 million, down from 117,000 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Js Capital Management Llc who had been investing in Facebook Inc for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $535.28B market cap company. The stock decreased 0.54% or $1.01 during the last trading session, reaching $184.92. About 9.79M shares traded. Facebook, Inc. (NASDAQ:FB) has risen 8.48% since May 27, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 3.07% the S&P500.
Stephen J. Errico decreased its stake in Star Group LP (SGU) by 3.41% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Locust Wood Capital Advisers Llc sold 34,126 shares as the company’s stock declined 11.39% with the market. The hedge fund run by Stephen J. Errico held 967,063 shares of the consumer services company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $10.40M, down from 1.00M at the end of the previous reported quarter. Locust Wood Capital Advisers Llc who had been investing in Star Group LP for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $501.78 million market cap company. The stock increased 0.54% or $0.05 during the last trading session, reaching $9.24. About 76,732 shares traded. Star Group, L.P. (NYSE:SGU) has risen 2.84% since May 27, 2017 and is uptrending. It has underperformed by 8.71% the S&P500.
Analysts await Facebook, Inc. (NASDAQ:FB) to report earnings on July, 25. They expect $1.72 earnings per share, up 30.30% or $0.40 from last year’s $1.32 per share. FB’s profit will be $4.98 billion for 26.88 P/E if the $1.72 EPS becomes a reality. After $1.69 actual earnings per share reported by Facebook, Inc. for the previous quarter, Wall Street now forecasts 1.78% EPS growth.
